title: Degreewise finite open exchange under restriction of scalars
statement: For a cartesian open-immersion square and a homomorphism of finite commutative rings, the canonical source scalar identification followed by the restricted C-coefficient open exchange equals the B-coefficient open exchange followed by the canonical target scalar identification, on every C-module sheaf.

source.place: Degreewise component of the returned Step 7 finite exchange before lifting to complexes.

proof.text: The direct-image coefficient comparison is identity on every section. Apply the mate equivalence for the normalized module inverse-image adjunctions to compare successive pullback scalar maps with the composite map. The conjugates of moduleGComp are moduleRComp; their section formulas both use the same pullbackComp restriction. Paste the two composition identities along the commuting square, using moduleSquareG_eq, to obtain pullRes_square. The generic mateSquare and pasteTransport proofs are reused from the ordinary restriction/pullback module, at the coefficient universe of this statement.

source.place: Degreewise component of the returned Step 7 finite exchange before lifting to complexes.

proof.text: Apply the open-extension adjunction homEquiv to both inverse exchange composites and cancel the invertible pullRes component. Naturality moves the scalar comparisons past the open unit and inverse exchange. The mate-unit identity identifies the scalar-restricted unit; the defining homEquiv equation for singleBetaInv identifies the adjunct of beta.inv. Naturality of moduleSquareG followed by pullRes_square makes the two adjuncts equal. Injectivity of homEquiv proves equality of inverse composites. Postcompose the desired forward square with the restricted inverse exchange and use the inverse identities to obtain the statement.
